title: Lift a can out of a drawer divider row
instruction: Take the soup can out of the drawer and leave it standing in the marked area beside it.
context: Deep kitchen drawers often hold cans upright in single rows between drawer dividers. A can stored in such a row sits below the divider tops, so it has to be taken straight out from above: the gripper must first turn to line up with the slot, because its fingers only fit into a space a few millimetres wider than they are, then reach down, grip the can, lift it clear of the dividers and set it upright on the counter. There is no cord or handle to pull; the hand itself has to fit into the confined space.
setup: One standard soup can, diameter 67.7 mm, height 101.9 mm and mass 450 g, stands at world (0.160, +0.100) m on the floor of an open deep kitchen drawer. The exact simulated can dimensions are diameter 67.66 mm and height 101.86 mm. Two fixed bamboo boards represent Lipper International model 8897 adjustable deep drawer dividers. Manufacturer specifications: thickness 15.875 mm, height 127 mm and adjustable length 460.375 to 558.8 mm; source: https://www.lipperinternational.com/products/bamboo-deep-drawer-dividers-set-of-two/. Product dimensions come from the manufacturer specification and have not been physically measured. The selected divider length is 460.375 mm, and the clear row width between their inner faces is 77.052 mm. The row axis is 7.971604 degrees from world +x. The can is at the row midpoint, 230.188 mm from each end frame inner face, 70 mm from the near side inner face and 230 mm from the opposite side inner face. The chosen drawer interior is 460.375 x 300 x 150 mm; four plywood frame boards are 18 mm thick, and the floor is 12 mm thick. These drawer dimensions are scenario choices. For exact board placement, use local coordinates (u, v, z) in mm, with origin at world (0.160, +0.100) m on the countertop, u along the row and v perpendicular to it. Divider centres: (0, -46.463522, 63.5) and (0, +46.463522, 63.5), each size (460.375, 15.875, 127). End-frame centres: (-239.1875, -80, 75) and (+239.1875, -80, 75), each size (18, 336, 150). Side-frame centres: (0, -239, 75) and (0, +79, 75), each size (460.375, 18, 150). Floor centre: (0, -80, -6), size (496.375, 336, 12). All seven boards are fixed. The drawer floor and countertop share the station table plane. Four fixed pale strips form a 110 mm square landing outline centred at world (0.240, +0.280) m: two 2 x 110 x 0.5 mm strips centred at x=0.186 and 0.294 m, y=0.280 m; two 106 x 2 x 0.5 mm strips centred at x=0.240 m, y=0.226 and 0.334 m. Strip centres are 0.25 mm above the countertop and their edges follow world x and y. The can starts 1 mm above the floor and settles. The left arm works on the positive-y side; the right arm starts at its raised ready pose. No cord, handle or tool is present.
scoring: Highest satisfied tier, evaluated at the end: 0.25 after a continuous upright lift puts the can bottom at least 3 mm above the 127 mm divider tops (130 mm above the drawer floor), followed by the can being wholly outside the drawer and upright; 0.50 if it also stands on the countertop with its bottom from 1 mm below to 2 mm above the surface, both grippers open by at least 85 mm and both complete hand envelopes at least 30 mm away; 0.75 if its centre is also within 15 mm on both world x and y axes of (0.240, +0.280) m and every pair of positions in the last 10 control frames is within 2 mm. Upright means tilt below 5 degrees. Full conditions held for 1.0 s earn 1.0. Before the 10-frame window fills, stillness requires speed below 10 mm/s and spin below 0.2 rad/s. The extraction height measures removal from the divider row; the fixed outer frame physically constrains the transfer. Any observed part of the can outside the countertop bounds x=[-0.19, 0.91] m or y=[-0.65, 0.65] m, or a bottom more than 10 mm below the surface, irreversibly yields zero. Tilt and misplaced landings can be repaired. No witnessed extraction, an invalid initial layout, missing object state or changed fixed geometry yields zero; missing hand readings prevent release credit. A direct jump to the final pose without a continuous upward crossing earns zero. Divider contact is not a scoring condition.
reset_notes: Restore the can upright to its stated row midpoint and reset both arms. Fixed drawer boards remain in place. A fresh episode clears history; an in-place reset is recognized only after a can-position jump greater than 100 mm into the complete nominal layout. Slow physical restoration does not clear an off-countertop latch.
fidelity: The can is represented in simulation by a rigid cylinder with the stated dimensions and mass; the drawer floor and countertop are coplanar.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (800/800 steps, max_steps); demo: 1.0 (279 steps, success)
